context.objective: Document how we carry out Analytical Review & Allocation Recalculations, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: It kicks off during quarterly close, once the numbers are ready to be tested.
Talk me through how you test the numbers and carry out the allocation recalculations during quarterly close?
We basically review the balances and then redo the allocations ourselves to see if they match what was booked.
What inputs and allocation basis do you use when you redo the allocations?
Independent support, not the file that produced the booked number.
What does the independent support provide for your recalculation?

Let me be precise. As the Fund Accountant, the preparer, I do it in this order. First I define the review population and sources: I list the balances and allocations to be tested, identify an independent source for every input, document why each source is independent of the booked result, and confirm the population includes current joiners, leavers and vesting changes. That gives me a test plan, a source index and a validated population. If no independent source exists for an input I stop and escalate to the Controller; the alternative compensating test is not defined yet, so I do not know what it would be. Second, in the analytical review workpaper, I compare balance sheet accounts and accruals to prior periods, evaluate movements for completeness and consistency with known activity, consider fund lifecycle timing, and investigate anything inconsistent, incomplete, unsupported or mistimed. There is no approved variance threshold, so the Controller decides how deep the investigation goes. Third, in the allocation recalculation workpaper in Excel, I recompute contributions and distributions from underlying support, recompute partners capital and P and L allocations, compare my results to the booked amounts, and classify each difference as an input, population, method, timing or ledger-recording issue and document the source. The percentages must come from the approved LPA-based documentation, never from the allocation file being tested. Every unexplained difference is corrected or escalated; there is no approved materiality threshold.
How do you verify a difference after its correction is made?

The Controller reviews them. The Controller challenges independence, completeness and the conclusions and can require correction or additional evidence. After that the Director does a final close review, depending on complexity. Who formally approves this review, and who has authority over an unresolved or immaterial difference, is not confirmed, so I do not know. But the package does not go to the Controller straight after the allocation recalculation; three more tests come first, all done by me as Fund Accountant. Fourth step, same-commitment and population checks: I compare PCAP and unfunded commitment balances for investors with identical commitments, they should be identical, and I confirm joiners, leavers, vesting changes and reallocations are reflected. A valid difference has to be explained with governing support; if balances differ without that, the Controller and the client decide and we either prove the governing difference or correct the allocation, and population issues get routed back to the upstream teams. Fifth step, carry: I build the Income Test from independently tested workpapers, not system carry balances, recompute carry life to date from fund inception, subtract carry recorded in prior periods to get the current period amount, and compare it to recorded carry. If it does not reconcile I recheck the life to date calculation, prior period carry, the population and the distribution waterfall, and waterfall method questions go to the waterfall team using the client-approved LPA interpretation. Sixth step, only when applicable, special profits: I confirm the LPA authorizes the shift, recalculate available income independently, recalculate the shift, and compare to the recorded treatment and fund wind-down expectations. No shift is made unless the LPA available-income requirement is met, and the shift is on hold until the LPA provision plus Client, Tax, Legal and Accounting approvals are documented. Who owns that interpretation is not specified.
When the Controller requires a correction or additional evidence, how does that work return to you and get rechecked?

It is finished when no unexplained difference and no unsupported conclusion remains. Before the Controller review there is a seventh step that gets us there, done by me as Fund Accountant with the Controller reviewing: I classify each difference and obtain underlying support, correct errors through the applicable upstream process without overwriting the original test record, rerun the affected tests, write conclusions that cite prior-period consistency, population completeness, lifecycle timing or underlying support, since saying only reasonable is not enough, then submit the package for Controller review and keep the review record. Each exception goes in the exception log with its reason, source, effective period, approver and resolution. If a difference remains unresolved we stop and escalate to the Controller and Director; it blocks the allocation and close conclusion. There is no approved materiality policy, so a residual difference is resolved exactly or escalated, never just waved through as immaterial. The records we keep are the source index, analytical workpaper, recalculation files, population schedule, same-commitment test, Income Test, special-profit support, exception log, rerun test results, documented conclusions and the Controller review record, in the digital binder; the exact storage path and retention period are not specified, so I do not know them. Afterwards the results feed the downstream reporting processes, financial statements, capital accounts and close approval. The close calendar deadline date is not specified either.
What can go wrong downstream if an allocation error or unsupported conclusion is not caught in this review?
